content.text: {"kind":"summary","title":"Scoring abstention against content, not missing gold labels","claims":[{"claim_id":"c1","text":"Treating a context with no gold documents as unanswerable fails: 28% to 72% of no-gold contexts still contain the answer, and shortcut precision falls from .68 to .10 as retrievers improve.","handles":["e3d1959f2c680"],"section":"overview"},{"claim_id":"c2","text":"A Qwen3-4B reader answered 62-67% of these false misses correctly; the paper recommends scoring refusals against content labels rather than gold presence.","handles":["e350fc01cffdc","e9519b5bbe055"],"section":"overview"}],"abstention":null,"question":null,"proposal":"Bounded test: for one retriever, label each no-gold context by content with two LLM judges, blind-audit about 250 contexts, then score refusals against those labels instead of gold presence.","limitation":"The abstracts do not address poisoned claims that multiple retrieved documents agree on, so that part is unsupported."}
